 Local insurance agent breaks down what to know about 2027 health coverage
 Shawn Cabbagestalk 
 11 hours ago 
 AUGUSTA, Ga. (WJBF) — Choosing health insurance for 2027 could mean higher costs for some consumers. A local insurance agent says people should look beyond the monthly premium before renewing their coverage.
 Peter Menk, a licensed insurance agent who works with Medicare and Affordable Care Act plans, joined NewsChannel 6 to discuss what consumers should consider.
 “We’ve seen prices go up and up and up for quite a while now,” Menk said.
 He pointed to changes involving federal tax credits that help lower the cost of health insurance for eligible consumers.
 The enhanced ACA premium tax credits expired at the end of 2025. While some consumers can still qualify for the original tax credits, people with household incomes above 400% of the federal poverty level no longer qualify for that assistance.
 Menk said consumers should consider three things when comparing plans: affordability, access to care and protection against major medical expenses.
 First, make sure the monthly premium fits your budget. But Menk said a lower premium does not necessarily mean a plan is the best choice.
 “There’s no point in paying for something you can’t use,” he said.
 That means checking whether your doctors and other health care providers are in the plan’s network. Consumers should also make sure their prescriptions are covered.
 Menk said people can check a plan’s provider network and prescription drug formulary before enrolling.
 He also recommends looking at how much a plan would cover if you need hospitalization or surgery.
 “Those are critical for having a good health plan,” Menk said.
 For 2027, average benchmark silver premiums for Affordable Care Act Marketplace plans are increasing by 13% nationwide, according to an analysis by KFF. Actual costs vary by location, plan and individual circumstances.
 Menk also reminded consumers to pay attention to enrollment deadlines.
 Medicare’s annual open enrollment period runs through December 7. People with Medicare can use that time to review or change their Medicare Advantage or prescription drug coverage.
 For Affordable Care Act Marketplace coverage, open enrollment runs through January 15, 2027. Consumers who want coverage to begin January 1 must enroll by December 15.
 Menk said seniors should be careful about entering personal information on unfamiliar insurance websites.
 “Don’t fill out a form online,” he said, warning that submitting information can lead to calls from multiple insurance marketing companies.
 Consumers can contact Menk at 706-394-0786 for help reviewing their coverage options.
